headline: Go and Python, Kubernetes in production, and a Linux estate I run myself.
pitch: I write Go at DGRS Labs (buckt, and loom's agent engine) and wrote it earlier at Nirvana Labs. I write Python at Equity, where I built a loan service's APIs and reusable framework components, and at DGRS Labs for AI agents. At Equity I containerized services and deployed them via Kubernetes; at DGRS Labs I provision and run every Linux server myself.

matches.requirement: A Golang developer also fluent in Python
matches.evidence: Go: buckt, a Go media library at DGRS Labs, and ChainQuery, an Ethereum indexer I wrote in Go at Nirvana Labs. Python: the loan service's Django REST Framework APIs at Equity and open-source AI agents at DGRS Labs.
Containerized Equity's services with Docker and deployed them via Azure Pipelines and Kubernetes, with Redis for performance and reliability in production.
Provision and configure every Linux server at DGRS Labs, with scripts that restore the full stack automatically. buckt and Noewright are open Go libraries with public docs.
Defined the deployment rules and release process the whole DGRS Labs team follows, and guided Equity's engineers on service integration and business logic.

resume.summary: Lead software engineer with 5+ years building and running production systems, writing Go and Python throughout. Created buckt, a Go media library, created a Go engine for multi-agent applications, and single-handedly runs the company's Linux infrastructure and CI/CD. Previously led delivery of a Python USSD loan service, containerized and deployed via Kubernetes, on a financial platform serving 16 million customers in six countries.

note:
The role asks for a Go developer who is also fluent in Python and knows Kubernetes. I've written both languages across my career: Go at DGRS Labs and Nirvana Labs, Python at Equity and DGRS Labs. I've deployed on Kubernetes and I run Linux servers every day.

What I'd bring first is the operator's view: I build the software and then keep it running myself, so I care about how a thing is installed, upgraded and recovered as much as how it's written.

What would be new: I've used Kubernetes as a platform to deploy onto, not written operators or charms for it. I'm in Lagos, which suits EMEA hours, and the twice-yearly sprints in person are fine with me.
